clearedSpotChecks.check: L-1314. What ruint PR 603 changed, and whether the revm-interpreter 35.0.1, 37.0.3 and 43.0.2 handlers for SHL, SHR, SAR and BYTE bound the count or index before calling ruint.
clearedSpotChecks.note: Fetched https://raw.githubusercontent.com/recmo/uint/v1.20.0/CHANGELOG.md: line 22 lists #603 as the overflowing_shl and overflowing_shr flag fix, line 56 lists #574 as the shift optimisation. In bits.rs v1.18.0:374-376 wrapping_shl is overflowing_shl(rhs).0; in v1.19.0:437-451 the u64 and u128 paths call unbounded_shl(rhs as u32); in v1.20.0:464-478 they call unbounded_shl(shift_amount(rhs)). Downloaded https://static.crates.io/crates/revm-interpreter/revm-interpreter-35.0.1.crate: bitwise.rs byte, shl, shr and sar use as_usize_saturated (macros.rs:185-189, usize::try_from(v).unwrap_or(usize::MAX)) and call ruint only when shift < 256 or o1 < 32, so the truncating cast can never see a count of 2^32 or more. 37.0.3 and 43.0.2 were not re-read by me. On the code side I grepped every shl, shr, sar, byte, << and >> in src/: every count is a constant, a uint8 (TickBitmap.sol:73, 97, 110), msb-derived and below 256 (TickMath.sol:136-137), an f in {0,1} (TickMath.sol:145 and following), or x >> r after the binary search, which is at most 0xff (BitMath.sol:22); BitMath.sol:40 uses shl(2, shr(250, ..)) which is below 256. Extsload.sol:23 shifts a caller value by the constant 5, so the caller controls the operand, not the count. No line of src/ can pass a large count. Six edge vectors of my own (MULMOD, ADDMOD, SAR and SHR with count 2^32+1, SHL 255, SDIV of MIN by -1, SIGNEXTEND 0) in clientVersion-bracketed batches returned the specified words on polygon-bor-rpc.publicnode.com (builds 280514fa9fb7 and f2a2d63e69f6), forno.celo.org (reth 74cc8bb) and bsc-dataseed1.bnbchain.org (Geth v1.8.2-4e1c8247), both brackets equal in all nine batches.

clearedSpotChecks.check: Task 2 (L-1315). polygon-bor-rpc.publicnode.com, every vector and script tied to each of the five bor builds; only the 39 known gas-limited scripts differ.
clearedSpotChecks.note: out/pin-polygon-ops.json records 0 mismatches and 132 of 132 jobs for each of the five builds. I ran three bracketed batches on the endpoint myself; two builds answered and each batch had equal brackets, so pinning by bracket holds. I tested the gas explanation for the 39 differing scripts, because a Polygon-only execution difference in swaps would be the costliest thing this item could hide. pmdiff.py:186 runs every script at gas 25,000,000 on all networks. Measured with the GAS opcode at that limit, a cold SLOAD costs 5,467 gas including 7 gas of overhead on Polygon and 2,107 on Ethereum (reth v2.11.0), and an SSTORE to a new slot costs 22,948 against 22,108. TSTORE, KECCAK256 and a cold CALL cost the same. Polygon storage reads cost more, so a long multi-tick swap runs out of gas at a limit that is enough on Ethereum, as opcodes/pmdiff-gas.json and OPCODES.md:60 state. With no gas field, Polygon's eth_call grants about 2^63 gas and Ethereum's 50,000,000. src/ has no branch on gasleft; gas() appears only as the forwarded amount in Currency.sol:48 and 73 and Hooks.sol:134. An out-of-gas failure reverts the whole transaction, which delays the swap and loses nothing. One small inconsistency: OPCODES.md:275 says four Polygon full-range swaps now complete at the higher cap. This item says the same 39 scripts differ at 25M gas, which is a different gas setting, so the two statements do not contradict each other. The per-build pmdiff and pmdiff2 results were not compared script by script against the stored 25M lists by me.

clearedSpotChecks.note: The probability arithmetic checks out: with p = 0.35 and q = 0.65, 1 - 0.35^28 - 0.65^28 = 0.999994 per chunk, and 0.999994^214 = 0.9988. The item correctly limits itself to a sampling statement and says that it covers no build that answers too rarely to appear among 5,992 bracket answers. The two op-reth builds (v2.8.1 and v0.0.0-dev-unknown) both use revm handlers of the kind read above, and the same vectors are already settled for OP Stack chains in OPCODES.md. I did not rerun the 28 rounds. Shift counts cannot exceed 255 in src/ (see the first spot check), so a rare build with a ruint 1.19 cast fault could not reach a PoolManager result even if one existed.
